s2.p1: No WDSF member federation. But on Lake Malawi’s southern shores, pairs dance **m’bwiza** at night, by a bonfire, to an ==accordion==.
s2.p2: One untested theory: Malawians working in European homes in the Rhodesias watched their employers dance ballroom, and took it home.

s3.p: of Gule Wamkulu are described in a book by Father **Claude Boucher** of Mua Mission. New ones keep coming: recent masks include ==Barack Obama== and Ebola.

s4.p1: A festival born in **2004** on the shores of Lake Malawi. About 700 people came the first year. At night, the beach is the dance floor.
s4.p2: Time Out called it ==possibly the most beautiful festival location in the world==. The 2025 edition was held in **Nkhotakota**.

s5.name: GULE WAMKULU
s5.p: The **Nyau**, a secret society of men, dance in wood and straw masks as spirits and animals: after the July harvest, at weddings and funerals.

s5.name: TCHOPA
s5.p: **20 to 30 dancers** criss-cross in a circle to three drums, to celebrate harvests and hunts, or as offerings to ancestors after droughts.

s6.p: Among the Tumbuka of the north, **Vimbuza** patients, mostly women, enter a trance to drums. In UNESCO’s words, they ==dance their disease==.

s7.p: **Gule Wamkulu** and **Vimbuza** are proclaimed UNESCO Masterpieces, listed in 2008. **Tchopa** (2014) and Mwinoghe (2018) follow.
s7.p2: Troupe **Rising Choreos** is invited to Festivals du Sud with 16 dances: one of only two African acts among 45.

sources.claim: M’bwiza: partner dance on southern Lake Malawi shores, at night by bonfire, accordion; Kwilimbe’s unresearched ‘hired hand’ theory (Malawians in European households in the Rhodesias watching employers dance ballroom)
WDSF African member list (DanceSport Africa) does not include Malawi
WDSF Southern Africa development coverage lists Botswana, Mozambique, Lesotho, South Africa, Namibia, Swaziland, not Malawi
Boucher’s book describes more than 200 Gule Wamkulu characters in seven themes
Father Claude Boucher at Mua Mission documented 400+ gule characters, 200+ masks; recent new characters include Barack Obama and Ebola
Lake of Stars founded 2004 on Lake Malawi shores; ~700 attendees at first edition; Time Out 2015 accolade
Time Out: ‘possibly the most beautiful festival location in the world’; beach overtaken by dancing at night; roots in Chibuku Shake Shake club night
Lake of Stars 2025 held 17–19 October at Fish Eagle Bay Lodge, Nkhotakota

Gule Wamkulu: Chewa, Nyau secret society of men, wood and straw masks, after July harvest, weddings, funerals; said to date to 17th-century Chewa Empire; Malawi, Zambia, Mozambique; proclaimed 2005, inscribed 2008
Tchopa, Lhomwe of southern Malawi: 20–30 dancers in a circle criss-crossing, three drums, after harvests/hunts and offerings after droughts; inscribed 2014
Vimbuza healing dance: Tumbuka of northern Malawi, patients mostly women, trance, drums, patients ‘dance their disease’; proclaimed 2005, inscribed 2008
Rising Choreos invited to 2024 Festivals du Sud, France: 16 dances, one of two African acts among 45 participants
